title: Neural associations between fingerspelling, print, and signs: An ERP priming study with deaf readers
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from an ERP priming study investigating neural associations between fingerspelling, print, and signs in deaf readers. Participants viewed prime-target pairs consisting of English words, ASL signs, or fingerspelled words followed by English word targets, allowing examination of cross-modal semantic priming effects. The study was conducted at San Diego State University's NeuroCognition Laboratory.
methods_description: Participants sat in a darkened, sound-attenuated room and viewed stimuli on an LCD monitor at 150cm viewing distance. They were presented with 300 prime-target pairs (100 English word primes, 100 ASL sign primes, 100 fingerspelled word primes), half related and half unrelated to targets. Each trial began with a purple fixation cross (800ms), then a white cross (500ms), followed by the prime stimulus (300ms for words, variable duration for ASL and fingerspelled videos) and a 4-letter English word target (500ms). Participants pressed a gamepad button upon detecting an animal stimulus across any modality.
